page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16 variants, and AES cryptography support.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg7.2xlarge primarily in the average performance tier. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1254.0 and a multi-core score of 4891.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 9399.28. Memory performance is stable, with a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 463.02 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds of 34.66 GB/sec. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in specific workloads, falling into the bottom 25% for bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU physics tests. Large-scale language model inference is a notable bottleneck, with medium 7B model prompt processing and text generation scoring in the bottom 10% of tested systems.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.hfg7.2xlarge offers a standard general-purpose hardware profile with dedicated compute resources, avoiding the performance fluctuations of shared-core instances. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average benchmark scores, it is well-suited for moderate workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 7.0 GB/sec, and Redis database operations, processing 7.65 million SET operations per second. It is also appropriate for software compilation and general text processing, though it is less optimal for heavy physics simulations, image processing, or local LLM deployment.
